To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human red cell anion exchange system is intrinsively asymmetric, such that in the absence of an anion gradient most of the unloaded anion transport sites face the intracellular side of the membrane, and that NAP-taurin is an excellent inhibitor that can be used to monitor the conformational changes of the anion exchange system and therefore to determine the fraction of sites in the outward-facing conformation.
NAP-taurines binds to the chloride transport site only when the transport site faces outward and the transport system is asymmetric.
the chloride gradient causes an asymmetric distribution of unloaded transport sites in the human red cell anion exchange system, and that this asymmetry is intrinsic to the transport system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the anion exchange system in human red cells.
the effects of the transport site on the binding of NAP-tau rine to its site.
the molecular mechanism of anion exchange.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chloride transport site is in an outward-facing conformational state (Eo ) about 80% of the time when the chloride gradient is zero.
the anion exchange system is intrinsively asymmetric, and that external NAP-tau-rine binds to its site only when the transport site faces the extracellular side.
the anion exchanger is intrinsically asymmetrical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transport site is intrinsically asymmetrical and that the binding site for external NAP-tau rine is located on the cytoplasmically facing side.
the human red cell chloride transport system is asymmetric with the majority of the unloaded transport site facing the cytoplasm.

the transport system can exist in two conformations, EClo and ECli, that are in rapid equilibrium with each other and that the binding site for external NAP-ta urine only binds when the transport site exists in the outward-facing conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anion exchange system is intrinsicaly asymmetric.
the transport system has two distinct conformational states that are separated from each other by a large free energy difference (DeltaG greater than 6.0 kcal/mol).
NAP-taurin can be used to measure the fraction of transporters that face outward.
